raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A server started with --prefill-max-requests 0 finishes startup, then never serves its first request, so generate() hangs. The scheduler stops adding requests to a batch once it holds the limit, and an empty batch already holds 0, so nothing is admitted. Negative values behave the same way, and main accepts both. Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23788, which recorded the hang on a live GPU server. @rahul-k-r confirmed that main still has the bug in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23826#issuecomment-6506409265.

## Modifications

The server now refuses to start when the limit is 0 or negative, and the message says the limit must be positive. Unset and positive limits behave as before.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This validates a configuration value and does not touch model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. Valid configurations run the same scheduler path.

## Testing Done

CPU only, macOS. The script resolves ServerArgs, the step every launch runs before model setup. The first run is on current main and the second on this branch. The GPU hang itself is recorded in the linked issue and was not rerun here.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer source: repro.py</summary>

```python
from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs

for value in (0, -1):
    try:
        ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", prefill_max_requests=value).resolve_once()
        print(f"prefill_max_requests={value}: accepted")
    except ValueError as exc:
        print(f"prefill_max_requests={value}: rejected: {exc}")
```

</details>

```text
$ git switch --detach 974831643f
$ TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1 PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python repro.py 2>/dev/null
prefill_max_requests=0: accepted
prefill_max_requests=-1: accepted
$ git switch 1fanwang/prefill-max-requests-positive
$ TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1 PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python repro.py 2>/dev/null
prefill_max_requests=0: rejected: --prefill-max-requests must be positive when set.
prefill_max_requests=-1: rejected: --prefill-max-requests must be positive when set.
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). One test covers the new check.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed, the error message states the valid range.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable, this is configuration validation.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
